source.text: אַ֣לְלַי לִ֗י כִּ֤י הָיִ֨יתִי֙ כְּאָסְפֵּי־קַ֔יִץ כְּעֹלְלֹ֖ת בָּצִ֑יר אֵין־אֶשְׁכּ֣וֹל לֶאֱכ֔וֹל בִּכּוּרָ֖ה אִוְּתָ֥ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe to me! For I have become like [the] gatherings of summer fruit, like [the] gleanings of [the] grape harvest; there is no cluster to eat, [no] early fig [which] my soul craves.

en.L: Woe [is] me! For I have become like the gatherings of summer fruit, \q like the gleanings of the grape harvest; \q there is no cluster to eat, \q no early fig [that] my soul craves.
en.B: Woe is me! I am like one who comes when the summer fruit is gathered, \q when the grape harvest has been gleaned: \q not a cluster of grapes is left to eat, \q not one of the early figs I long for.
en.R: How terrible this is for me! \q I am like someone who goes to pick fruit after the harvest is over. \q There are no grapes left to eat, \q none of the early figs I long for.

pt.L: Ai de mim! Pois fiquei como as colheitas de frutos de verão, \q como os restos da vindima; \q não há cacho para comer, \q nem figo temporão [que] a minha alma deseja.
pt.B: Ai de mim! Sou como quem chega quando os frutos de verão já foram colhidos, \q quando a vindima já foi rebuscada: \q não sobrou um cacho de uvas para comer, \q nem um dos primeiros figos que tanto desejo.
pt.R: Que desgraça é esta para mim! \q Sou como alguém que vai colher frutas depois que a colheita acabou. \q Não sobrou nenhuma uva para comer, \q nenhum dos primeiros figos que tanto desejo.

decisions.choice: Woe is me: a cry of grief over one's own state
decisions.reason: The word is a rare cry of lament, found elsewhere only in Job 10:15. The speaker is the prophet, mourning over his people, though some hear Zion herself speaking, as she does openly in verses 8-10.

decisions.choice: like the gatherings of summer fruit: like a picker who comes after the harvest and finds nothing
decisions.reason: After the harvest and the gleaning, nothing is left on the trees and vines. So it is with the people: the prophet looks for one faithful person and finds none (verse 2). Jeremiah 5:1 searches Jerusalem the same way, and Isaiah 24:13 uses the picture of the gleaning.

decisions.choice: an early fig: the first ripe figs, a prized delicacy
decisions.reason: The first figs of the season ripen in early summer and were eagerly sought (Isaiah 28:4; Hosea 9:10). "My soul craves" means "I long for": the self, with all its desire.

decisions.choice: Woe [is] me (L); Woe is me (B); How terrible this is for me (R); the gatherings of summer fruit (L); one who comes when the summer fruit is gathered (B); someone who goes to pick fruit after the harvest is over (R)
decisions.reason: The cry follows the wording set for the prophets' "woe" said of oneself. Balanced and Readable say what the likeness means (m2).

source.text: אָבַ֤ד חָסִיד֙ מִן־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְיָשָׁ֥ר בָּאָדָ֖ם אָ֑יִן כֻּלָּם֙ לְדָמִ֣ים יֶאֱרֹ֔בוּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־אָחִ֖יהוּ יָצ֥וּדוּ חֵֽרֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: Has perished [the] faithful from the land, and upright among humankind there is none; all of them for blood lie in wait; each his brother they hunt [with] a net.

en.L: The faithful has perished from the land, \q and there is no upright [one] among humankind; \q all of them lie in wait for blood; \q each hunts his brother [with] a net.
en.B: The faithful have vanished from the land; \q there is not one upright person left. \q They all lie in wait to shed blood; \q they hunt one another with nets.
en.R: Faithful people have disappeared from the land. \q There is no one left who does what is right. \q Everyone is waiting for a chance to kill. \q They set traps for one another.

pt.L: O fiel pereceu da terra, \q e não há [nenhum] reto entre os seres humanos; \q todos eles armam emboscadas por sangue; \q cada um caça o seu irmão [com] rede.
pt.B: Os fiéis desapareceram da terra; \q não sobrou nenhuma pessoa reta. \q Todos ficam de tocaia para derramar sangue; \q caçam uns aos outros com redes.
pt.R: As pessoas fiéis desapareceram da terra. \q Não sobrou ninguém que faça o que é certo. \q Todos estão esperando uma chance de matar. \q Eles armam armadilhas uns para os outros.

decisions.choice: the faithful: the person who keeps loyal love
decisions.reason: The word is formed from *hesed*, loyal love (6:8). The faithful person is one who keeps faith with God and with others. None is left: this is the empty harvest of verse 1.

decisions.choice: lie in wait for blood: plot to kill or ruin others
decisions.reason: The words describe robbers waiting in ambush (Proverbs 1:11, 18). The prophet means not only murder but the ruin of the weak by the powerful, which he calls bloodshed (3:10).

decisions.choice: each hunts his brother with a net: they prey on one another
decisions.reason: "Each ... his brother" is the Hebrew way of saying "one another". The net is a hunter's or fowler's trap (Psalm 140:6). People treat their own kin as game to be caught.

decisions.choice: The faithful has (L); The faithful have (B); Faithful people (R); each hunts his brother (L); they hunt one another (B); They set traps for one another (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "each ... his brother"; Balanced and Readable give its sense, "one another", which includes men and women (m3).

source.text: עַל־הָרַ֤ע כַּפַּ֨יִם֙ לְהֵיטִ֔יב הַשַּׂ֣ר שֹׁאֵ֔ל וְהַשֹּׁפֵ֖ט בַּשִׁלּ֑וּםוְהַגָּד֗וֹל דֹּבֵ֨ר הַוַּ֥ת נַפְשׁ֛וֹ ה֖וּא וַֽיְעַבְּתֽוּהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: On the evil [are] both hands, to do [it] well; the official asks, and the judge for a bribe, and the great one speaks [the] desire of his soul, he; and they weave it.

en.L: Both hands [are] on evil, to do [it] well; \q the official asks, \q and the judge [asks] for a bribe; \q and the great man speaks the desire of his soul, and they weave it together.
en.B: Their hands are skilled at doing evil; \q the official makes demands, \q the judge asks for a bribe, \q and the powerful man speaks out what he craves, and together they twist it.
en.R: They are experts at doing evil. \q The leaders demand gifts. \q The judges ask for bribes. \q Powerful people get what they want, and they all plot together.

pt.L: Ambas as mãos [estão] sobre o mal, para fazê-[lo] bem; \q o oficial pede, \q e o juiz [pede] suborno; \q e o grande fala o desejo da sua alma, e eles o tramam juntos.
pt.B: As mãos deles são hábeis em fazer o mal; \q o oficial faz exigências, \q o juiz pede suborno, \q e o poderoso diz o que cobiça, e juntos eles o torcem.
pt.R: Eles são especialistas em fazer o mal. \q Os líderes exigem presentes. \q Os juízes pedem suborno. \q Os poderosos conseguem o que querem, e todos tramam juntos.

decisions.choice: both hands on evil, to do it well: they are eager and skilled at wrongdoing
decisions.reason: Using both hands means giving full effort. "To do it well" is said with irony: the only thing they do well is evil. The Hebrew of the line is short and its exact construction uncertain, but the sense is clear.

decisions.choice: the official asks, and the judge for a bribe: justice is for sale
decisions.reason: Officials and judges were meant to protect the weak, and the law forbade bribes (Exodus 23:8; Deuteronomy 16:19). Here they demand payment (compare 3:11; Amos 5:12). "The great man" is the powerful noble who gets what he wants by saying so.

decisions.choice: they weave it together: they conspire
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here and seems to mean to twist or weave together. The official, the judge and the great man work together to get what each wants.

decisions.choice: official (L, B); leaders (R); great man (L); powerful man (B); Powerful people (R); weave it together (L); twist it (B); plot together (R)
decisions.reason: The word for official follows the wording set for the prophets. "Great man" and "powerful man" name one figure, a male noble; Readable makes the three figures plural, as a class.

source.text: טוֹבָ֣ם כְּחֵ֔דֶק יָשָׁ֖ר מִמְּסוּכָ֑ה י֤וֹם מְצַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ פְּקֻדָּתְךָ֣ בָ֔אָה עַתָּ֥ה תִהְיֶ֖ה מְבוּכָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] best of them [is] like a brier, [the] upright more than a thorn hedge; [the] day of your watchmen, your punishment, has come; now will be their confusion.

en.L: The best of them [is] like a brier, \q the most upright worse than a thorn hedge. \q The day of your watchmen, your punishment, has come; \q now their confusion will be.
en.B: The best of them is like a brier, \q the most upright worse than a hedge of thorns. \q The day your watchmen warned of has come, the day of your punishment; \q now is the time of their confusion.
en.R: Even the best of them are like thorny weeds. \q The most honest of them are worse than a hedge of thorns. \q The day your prophets warned you about has come. God is going to punish you. \q Now everyone will be confused and afraid.

pt.L: O melhor deles [é] como um espinheiro, \q o mais reto, pior que uma cerca de espinhos. \q O dia das tuas sentinelas, o teu castigo, chegou; \q agora será a confusão deles.
pt.B: O melhor deles é como um espinheiro, \q o mais reto, pior que uma cerca de espinhos. \q Chegou o dia de que as tuas sentinelas avisaram, o dia do teu castigo; \q agora é o tempo da confusão deles.
pt.R: Até os melhores deles são como mato cheio de espinhos. \q Os mais honestos são piores que uma cerca de espinhos. \q Chegou o dia de que os teus profetas te avisaram. Deus vai te castigar. \q Agora todos vão ficar confusos e com medo.

decisions.choice: like a brier ... a thorn hedge: they wound anyone who comes near
decisions.reason: A brier and a thorn hedge scratch and tear whoever touches them. Even the best of these people are like that: dealing with them brings only harm.

decisions.choice: the day of your watchmen: the day the prophets warned of
decisions.reason: Prophets are called watchmen, who look out and warn of danger (Jeremiah 6:17; Ezekiel 3:17; Hosea 9:8). The day they warned of is the day of punishment, and it has come. "Your" is singular, spoken to the people as one.

decisions.choice: their confusion: the panic of a people in disaster
decisions.reason: The word means confusion and dismay, as when an army is thrown into panic (Isaiah 22:5).

decisions.choice: The day your watchmen warned of ... the day of your punishment (B); The day your prophets warned you about ... God is going to punish you (R); confused and afraid (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the day of your watchmen" means (m2); Readable names the watchmen as prophets and God as the one who punishes.

source.text: אַל־תַּאֲמִ֣ינוּ בְרֵ֔עַ אַֽל־תִּבְטְח֖וּ בְּאַלּ֑וּף מִשֹּׁכֶ֣בֶת חֵיקֶ֔ךָ שְׁמֹ֖ר פִּתְחֵי־פִֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not believe in a neighbor; do not trust in a close friend; from her who lies in your bosom guard [the] openings of your mouth.

en.L: Do not believe in a neighbor; \q do not trust in a close friend; \q from her who lies in your bosom \q guard the doors of your mouth.
en.B: Do not trust a neighbor; \q put no confidence in a friend. \q Even with the woman who lies in your arms, \q guard the doors of your mouth.
en.R: Do not trust your neighbors. \q Do not depend on your friends. \q Be careful what you say, \q even to your own wife.

pt.L: Não creiam no próximo; \q não confiem no amigo íntimo; \q daquela que se deita no teu seio \q guarda as portas da tua boca.
pt.B: Não confiem no vizinho; \q não ponham a confiança no amigo. \q Até com a mulher que dorme nos teus braços, \q guarda as portas da tua boca.
pt.R: Não confiem nos seus vizinhos. \q Não dependam dos seus amigos. \q Tenham cuidado com o que dizem, \q até mesmo à própria esposa.

decisions.choice: her who lies in your bosom: one's own wife
decisions.reason: The phrase names the closest of all relationships (Deuteronomy 13:7, "the wife of your bosom"). When even she cannot be trusted with a secret, society has fallen apart.

decisions.choice: guard the doors of your mouth: be careful what you say
decisions.reason: The mouth is pictured as a door to be guarded (Psalm 141:3). In a society of informers, a careless word could be used against the speaker.

decisions.choice: her who lies in your bosom (L); the woman who lies in your arms (B); your own wife (R); doors of your mouth (L, B); Be careful what you say (R)
decisions.reason: The warning is spoken to a man, so "her" is his wife; Readable says so (m1) and explains the guarded door (m2).

decisions.choice: vocês, then tu (L, B); vocês throughout (R)
decisions.reason: The first two commands are plural and the last singular, spoken to each man about his wife (m1); Literal and Balanced keep the change of number, and Readable, which speaks to everyone, says "vocês" throughout.

source.text: כִּֽי־בֵן֙ מְנַבֵּ֣ל אָ֔ב בַּ֚ת קָמָ֣ה בְאִמָּ֔הּ כַּלָּ֖ה בַּחֲמֹתָ֑הּ אֹיְבֵ֥י אִ֖ישׁ אַנְשֵׁ֥י בֵיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For a son treats with contempt a father; a daughter rises up against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; [the] enemies of a man [are the] men of his house.

en.L: For a son treats [his] father with contempt, \q a daughter rises up against her mother, \q a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; \q the enemies of {{gender:a person|a man}} [are] the {{gender:people|men}} of {{gender:their|his}} own house.
en.B: For a son treats his father with contempt, \q a daughter rises against her mother, \q a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; \q {{gender:a person's|a man's}} enemies are the {{gender:people|men}} of {{gender:their|his}} own household.
en.R: Sons treat their fathers like fools. \q Daughters turn against their mothers, \q and daughters-in-law against their mothers-in-law. \q Your enemies are the people in your own family.

pt.L: Pois o filho despreza o pai, \q a filha se levanta contra a sua mãe, \q a nora contra a sua sogra; \q os inimigos {{gender:da pessoa|do homem}} [são] {{gender:as pessoas|os homens}} da sua casa.
pt.B: Pois o filho trata o pai com desprezo, \q a filha se levanta contra a mãe, \q a nora contra a sogra; \q os inimigos de cada um são os da sua própria casa.
pt.R: Os filhos tratam os pais como tolos. \q As filhas se voltam contra as mães, \q e as noras contra as sogras. \q Os inimigos de uma pessoa são as pessoas da própria família dela.

decisions.choice: son against father ... a man's enemies are his own household: words Jesus takes up in Matthew 10:35-36
decisions.reason: Jesus says that he has come to set a man against his father, a daughter against her mother and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law, and that a person's enemies will be those of his own household (Matthew 10:35-36; compare Luke 12:53). He uses Micah's words to describe the division that following him will bring even within families. In Micah they describe a society where every bond of trust has broken.

decisions.choice: treats with contempt: treats as a fool, dishonors
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for a fool, one who has no regard for God or for what is right (Deuteronomy 32:15; Psalm 14:1). The son breaks the command to honor father and mother (Exodus 20:12).

decisions.choice: a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law: the household that should have been one
decisions.reason: A married son and his wife usually lived in his parents' household. The "men of his house" are all who belong to it, men and women alike. The family, the first place of loyalty, has become a place of enemies.

decisions.choice: the enemies of a person ... the people of their own house (with the gender setting, L, B); Your enemies ... your own family (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "man" and "men of his house" mean any person and all the members of a household, so Literal and Balanced have the gender setting. Readable says "your", meaning anyone. Readable makes the three pairs plural.

decisions.choice: a filha contra a (sua) mãe, a nora contra a (sua) sogra; os inimigos da pessoa / de cada um / de uma pessoa ... os da sua (própria) casa, as Matthew 10:35-36
alternatives: os inimigos do homem são os da sua casa (L, B)
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up these words in Matthew 10:35-36 (m1), and each level keeps the Portuguese of Matthew's verses where the Hebrew is the same. The first line follows the Hebrew, where the son despises his father (m2), not Matthew's "set against". Balanced's "cada um" already means anyone, so it has no gender span, as in Matthew 10:36; Literal keeps the English setting on "da pessoa" and "as pessoas".

source.text: וַאֲנִי֙ בַּיהוָ֣ה אֲצַפֶּ֔ה אוֹחִ֖ילָה לֵאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעִ֑י יִשְׁמָעֵ֖נִי אֱלֹהָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: But I, for Yahweh I will watch; I will wait for [the] God of my salvation; my God will hear me.

en.L: But as for me, I will watch for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q I will hope for the God of my salvation; \q my God will hear me.
en.B: But I will keep watch for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q I will put my hope in the God who saves me; \q my God will hear me.
en.R: But I will look to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help. \q I will wait for God to save me. \q My God will hear me.

pt.L: Mas eu, eu esperarei atento {{divine_name:pelo SENHOR|por Javé}}; \q aguardarei o Deus da minha salvação; \q o meu Deus me ouvirá.
pt.B: Mas eu ficarei de vigia, à espera {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; \q porei a minha esperança no Deus que me salva; \q o meu Deus me ouvirá.
pt.R: Mas eu vou olhar {{divine_name:para o SENHOR|para Javé}} em busca de ajuda. \q Vou esperar que Deus me salve. \q O meu Deus vai me ouvir.

decisions.choice: But as for me: the turning point of the chapter
decisions.reason: In a land where no one can be trusted (verses 2-6), the speaker turns to the one who can be. The words "but as for me" set him against everything before, as in 3:8. From here the chapter moves from lament to trust and praise.

decisions.choice: I will watch ... I will wait: look out with expectation for the LORD to act
decisions.reason: The first verb is the work of a watchman (verse 4) looking out from a tower; the second means to wait in hope (Psalm 130:5-6; Habakkuk 2:1). The prophet watches, not for disaster, but for the LORD's salvation.

decisions.choice: watch for (L); keep watch for (B); look to ... for help (R); the God of my salvation (L, B); God to save me (R)
decisions.reason: The word for salvation follows the wording set for the prophets. Readable says what watching for the LORD means (m2).

source.text: אַֽל־תִּשְׂמְחִ֤י אֹיַ֨בְתִּי֙ לִ֔י כִּ֥י נָפַ֖לְתִּי קָ֑מְתִּי כִּֽי־אֵשֵׁ֣ב בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ יְהוָ֖ה א֥וֹר לִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Do not rejoice, my enemy, over me; though I have fallen, I will rise; though I sit in darkness, Yahweh [is] a light for me.

en.L: Do not rejoice over me, my enemy; \q though I have fallen, I will rise; \q though I sit in darkness, \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] a light for me.
en.B: Do not gloat over me, my enemy! \q I have fallen, but I will rise. \q Though I sit in darkness, \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is my light.
en.R: My enemy, do not laugh at me! \q I have fallen, but I will get up again. \q I am sitting in darkness, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be my light.

pt.L: Não te alegres sobre mim, inimiga minha; \q embora eu tenha caído, eu me levantarei; \q embora eu esteja sentada nas trevas, \q {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} [é] uma luz para mim.
pt.B: Não fiques contente com a minha queda, minha inimiga! \q Eu caí, mas vou me levantar. \q Embora eu esteja sentada nas trevas, \q {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} é a minha luz.
pt.R: Minha inimiga, não rias de mim! \q Eu caí, mas vou me levantar de novo. \q Estou sentada no escuro, \q mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vai ser a minha luz.

decisions.choice: my enemy: Zion speaks to a rival city, both pictured as women
decisions.reason: In verses 8-10 the speaker is Zion, the people of God, and "my enemy" is feminine: a hostile nation or city, pictured as a woman, which gloats over her fall. The text does not name it; Babylon, Edom and Nineveh have all been suggested.

decisions.choice: darkness ... light: distress, and the LORD's rescue
decisions.reason: Darkness is a picture of disaster and captivity, light of rescue and life (Psalm 27:1; Isaiah 9:1). Zion has fallen and sits in the dark, but she does not despair.

decisions.choice: rejoice over (L); gloat over (B); laugh at (R); [is] a light for me (L); is my light (B); will be my light (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the enemy's joy is: gloating over another's fall. The Hebrew has no verb in the last line; Readable puts it in the future, as the promise it is.

decisions.choice: minha inimiga, addressed as "tu"; sentada (feminine)
decisions.reason: In verses 8-10 Zion speaks, and the enemy she addresses is feminine (m1); Portuguese can keep both with "inimiga" and the speaker's "sentada", and the city addressed takes "tu".

source.text: זַ֤עַף יְהוָה֙ אֶשָּׂ֔א כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אתִי ל֑וֹ עַד֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֤יב רִיבִי֙ וְעָשָׂ֣ה מִשְׁפָּטִ֔י יוֹצִיאֵ֣נִי לָא֔וֹר אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּצִדְקָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] rage of Yahweh I will bear, for I have sinned against him, until he pleads my case and executes my justice; he will bring me out to the light; I will look on his righteousness.

en.L: I will bear the rage of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q for I have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} contends for my cause and does justice for me. \q He will bring me out into the light; \q I will gaze on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness.
en.B: I will bear the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q because I have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes up my case and wins justice for me. \q He will bring me out into the light, \q and I will see {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness.
en.R: I have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q so I must suffer {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} defends me and gives me justice. \q He will bring me out into the light, \q and I will see {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sets things right.

pt.L: Suportarei a fúria {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q porque pequei contra {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, \q até que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pleiteie a minha causa e me faça justiça. \q Ele me trará para fora, para a luz; \q contemplarei a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} retidão.
pt.B: Suportarei a ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q porque pequei contra {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, \q até que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} assuma a minha causa e me faça justiça. \q Ele me levará para a luz, \q e eu verei a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} retidão.
pt.R: Eu pequei contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q por isso tenho de sofrer a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira \q até que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me defenda e me faça justiça. \q Ele vai me levar para a luz, \q e eu vou ver a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} retidão, quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} puser tudo em ordem.

decisions.choice: I will bear the rage of the LORD, for I have sinned: Zion accepts his judgment as just
decisions.reason: Zion does not claim innocence. She owns her sin and bears the LORD's anger, trusting that it has an end (Lamentations 3:39-40; Isaiah 40:2). The same LORD who punishes will become her defender.

decisions.choice: until he pleads my case and executes justice for me: the LORD becomes her advocate
decisions.reason: The words are from the law court, as in 6:1-2. There the LORD had a case against his people; here he takes up their case against their enemies and gives them justice (Jeremiah 50:34; Lamentations 3:58-59).

decisions.choice: his righteousness: his faithfulness in setting things right for his people
decisions.reason: The LORD's righteousness here is not only that he is just, but his saving justice: the act by which he keeps his promises and puts his people in the right (Isaiah 46:13; 51:5). Zion will see it when he brings her out to the light.

decisions.choice: rage (L); anger (B, R); contends for my cause (L); takes up my case (B); defends me (R); righteousness (all levels); as he sets things right (R)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "righteousness" and adds what it means here (m3). "He" at the start of a sentence is capitalized either way.

decisions.choice: pleitear a causa (L); a retidão; fazer justiça
decisions.reason: As set for the prophets, tsedaqah is "retidão" and mishpat "justiça", so the LORD who "faz justiça" to Zion shows his "retidão" (m3). "Pleitear" keeps the court word of 6:1-2, where the case was against her (m2).

source.text: וְתֵרֶ֤א אֹיַ֨בְתִּי֙ וּתְכַסֶּ֣הָ בוּשָׁ֔ה הָאֹמְרָ֣ה אֵלַ֔י אַיּ֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יִךְ עֵינַי֙ תִּרְאֶ֣ינָּה בָּ֔הּ עַתָּ֛ה תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה לְמִרְמָ֖ס כְּטִ֥יט חוּצֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see my enemy, and will cover her shame, who says to me, Where [is] he, Yahweh your God? My eyes will look on her; now she will become a trampling place like [the] mud of [the] streets.

en.L: And my enemy will see, \q and shame will cover her \q who said to me, "Where [is] he, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God?" \q My eyes will look upon her; \q now she will be trampled like the mud of the streets.
en.B: Then my enemy will see it, \q and shame will cover her, \q she who taunted me, "Where is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God?" \q My eyes will watch her downfall; \q now she will be trodden down like mud in the streets.
en.R: My enemy will see it and be ashamed. \q She said to me, \q "Where is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God?" \q Now I will see her defeated. \q She will be trampled like mud in the streets.

pt.L: E a minha inimiga verá, \q e a vergonha a cobrirá, \q a que me dizia: "Onde [está] ele, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o teu Deus?" \q Os meus olhos olharão para ela; \q agora ela será pisada como a lama das ruas.
pt.B: Então a minha inimiga verá isso, \q e a vergonha a cobrirá, \q ela que zombava de mim: "Onde está {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o teu Deus?" \q Os meus olhos verão a queda dela; \q agora ela será pisada como lama nas ruas.
pt.R: A minha inimiga vai ver isso e ficar envergonhada. \q Ela me dizia: \q "Onde está {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o teu Deus?" \q Agora vou vê-la derrotada. \q Ela vai ser pisada como lama nas ruas.

decisions.choice: Where is the LORD your God? The taunt of the enemies of God's people
decisions.reason: The question mocks a people whose God seems to have left them (Psalm 42:4, 11; 79:10; Joel 2:17). The enemy's taunt will be answered: the LORD will act, and the shame will be hers.

decisions.choice: my eyes will look upon her: I will see her downfall
decisions.reason: In 4:11 the nations wanted their eyes to gaze on Zion's ruin. Now it is turned around: Zion will see the fall of the one who mocked her.

decisions.choice: trampled like the mud of the streets: utterly humbled
decisions.reason: Mud in the street is trodden underfoot by everyone. The same picture is used of a defeated enemy in Isaiah 10:6 and Zechariah 10:5.

decisions.choice: Where [is] he, the LORD your God? (L); Where is the LORD your God? (B, R); My eyes will look upon her (L); My eyes will see her downfall (B); I will see her defeated (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "Where is he?" is followed by the name; Literal keeps both. Balanced and Readable say what the look means (m2).

source.text: י֖וֹם לִבְנ֣וֹת גְּדֵרָ֑יִךְ י֥וֹם הַה֖וּא יִרְחַק־חֹֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: A day for building your walls! That day, far off will be [the] boundary.

en.L: A day for building your walls! \q In that day the boundary will be far off.
en.B: A day is coming for building your walls; \q on that day your boundary will be extended far.
en.R: The day will come when your walls will be rebuilt. \q At that time your borders will be made much wider.

pt.L: Dia de edificar os teus muros! \q Naquele dia o limite ficará longe.
pt.B: Vem um dia de reconstruir os teus muros; \q naquele dia as tuas fronteiras serão estendidas para longe.
pt.R: Vai chegar o dia em que os teus muros serão reconstruídos. \q Naquele tempo as tuas fronteiras vão ficar muito mais largas.

decisions.choice: A day for building your walls: a promise to Zion
decisions.reason: The prophet now speaks to Zion ("your" is feminine). The line has no verb: it announces a day. The walls that the enemy pulled down will be rebuilt, as Amos 9:11 promises and as Nehemiah later did.

decisions.choice: the boundary will be far off: the borders will be extended
alternatives: the decree will be far off: the enemy's rule will be removed
decisions.reason: The word usually means a decree or statute, and also a boundary or limit (Job 26:10). Here, with the building of walls and the coming of many peoples (verse 12), it most likely means that the city's boundary will be pushed far out. It may mean that the decree imposed by the enemy will be removed.

decisions.choice: A day for building (L); A day is coming for building (B); The day will come when (R); In that day (L); on that day (B); At that time (R); far off (L); extended far (B); made much wider (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb the Hebrew leaves out, and say what the far-off boundary means (m2). "That day" follows the wording set for the prophets.

source.text: י֥וֹם הוּא֙ וְעָדֶ֣יךָ יָב֔וֹא לְמִנִּ֥י אַשּׁ֖וּר וְעָרֵ֣י מָצ֑וֹר וּלְמִנִּ֤י מָצוֹר֙ וְעַד־נָהָ֔ר וְיָ֥ם מִיָּ֖ם וְהַ֥ר הָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: [In] that day, and to you will come, from Assyria and [the] cities of Egypt, and from Egypt even to [the] River, and sea from sea and mountain [to] the mountain.

en.L: [It will be] that day, and [people] will come to you \q from Assyria and [from] the cities of Egypt, \q and from Egypt as far as the River, \q and sea from sea, and mountain [to] the mountain.
en.B: On that day people will come to you \q from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, \q from Egypt as far as the Euphrates, \q from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.
en.R: At that time people will come to you \q from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, \q from Egypt all the way to the Euphrates River, \q from every sea and every mountain.

pt.L: [Será] aquele dia, e [gente] virá a ti \q da Assíria e [das] cidades do Egito, \q e do Egito até o Rio, \q e mar desde mar, e monte [até] o monte.
pt.B: Naquele dia, virá gente a ti \q da Assíria e das cidades do Egito, \q do Egito até o Eufrates, \q de mar a mar e de monte a monte.
pt.R: Naquele tempo, virá gente até ti \q da Assíria e das cidades do Egito, \q do Egito até o rio Eufrates, \q de todos os mares e de todos os montes.

decisions.choice: from Assyria ... Egypt ... the River ... sea to sea: from every corner of the known world
decisions.reason: Assyria and Egypt were the two great powers, one to the north-east and one to the south-west. "The River" is the Euphrates. "From sea to sea and mountain to mountain" means from one end of the earth to the other (Psalm 72:8; Zechariah 9:10). Those who come may be Israel's scattered people coming home (Isaiah 11:11; 27:13), or the nations coming to Zion (4:1-2).

decisions.choice: Egypt: a poetic name that also means "fortress"
decisions.reason: The word used here for Egypt is a rare poetic form (2 Kings 19:24; Isaiah 19:6), which is spelled like the word for a siege or fortress (4:14). Some read "the fortified cities"; the pairing with Assyria points to Egypt.

decisions.choice: the River (L); the Euphrates (B); the Euphrates River (R); people (B, R); from every sea and every mountain (R)
decisions.reason: The River follows the wording set for the prophets. The Hebrew "he will come" names no one; Balanced and Readable say "people". Readable gives the sense of "sea to sea, mountain to mountain" (m1).

source.text: וְהָיְתָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ לִשְׁמָמָ֖ה עַל־יֹֽשְׁבֶ֑יהָ מִפְּרִ֖י מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And will become the earth a desolation on account of its inhabitants, from [the] fruit of their deeds.

en.L: And the earth will become a desolation because of its inhabitants, \q because of the fruit of their deeds.
en.B: But the earth will become desolate because of those who live in it, \q as the result of what they have done.
en.R: But the earth will become empty and ruined \q because of the evil things its people have done.

pt.L: E a terra se tornará uma desolação por causa dos seus habitantes, \q por causa do fruto das suas obras.
pt.B: Mas a terra ficará desolada por causa dos que vivem nela, \q como resultado do que fizeram.
pt.R: Mas a terra vai ficar vazia e arruinada \q por causa das coisas más que o seu povo fez.

decisions.choice: the earth: the lands of the nations, judged while Zion is restored
alternatives: the land of Israel, before it is restored
decisions.reason: The word means the earth or a land. After the world-wide picture of verse 12, it most likely means the earth, the nations that refused to listen (5:14), which will be laid waste. Some read it as Israel's own land, left desolate for its people's sins before the restoration of verses 11-12.

decisions.choice: the fruit of their deeds: the result of what they have done
decisions.reason: What people do grows into what they reap (Jeremiah 17:10; 21:14; Proverbs 1:31). The desolation is not arbitrary; it is the harvest of their own deeds.

decisions.choice: And (L); But (B, R); the fruit of their deeds (L); what they have done (B); the evil things its people have done (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "but" to mark the contrast with the promise to Zion (m1), and give the sense of the picture of fruit (m2).

source.text: רְעֵ֧ה עַמְּךָ֣ בְשִׁבְטֶ֗ךָ צֹ֚אן נַֽחֲלָתֶ֔ךָ שֹׁכְנִ֣י לְבָדָ֔ד יַ֖עַר בְּת֣וֹךְ כַּרְמֶ֑ל יִרְע֥וּ בָשָׁ֛ן וְגִלְעָ֖ד כִּימֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Shepherd your people with your rod, [the] flock of your inheritance, dwelling alone, [in] a forest in [the] midst of Carmel; let them graze [in] Bashan and Gilead as [in the] days of old.

en.L: Shepherd {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} staff, the flock of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance, \q dwelling alone, \q [in] a forest in the midst of Carmel; \q let them graze [in] Bashan and Gilead as in ancient days.
en.B: Shepherd {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} staff, the flock that belongs to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q which lives alone \q in a forest in the middle of Carmel. \q Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as they did long ago.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, care for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people like a shepherd with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} staff. They are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own flock, \q living alone \q in a forest near the rich land of Carmel. \q Let them feed in Bashan and Gilead, as they did long ago.

pt.L: Apascenta o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo com o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} cajado, o rebanho da {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} herança, \q que habita sozinho, \q [num] bosque no meio do Carmelo; \q que pastem [em] Basã e Gileade como nos dias antigos.
pt.B: Apascenta o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo com o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} cajado, o rebanho que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pertence, \q que vive sozinho \q num bosque no meio do Carmelo. \q Que eles pastem em Basã e em Gileade, como faziam muito tempo atrás.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, cuida do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo como um pastor, com o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} cajado. Eles são o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} próprio rebanho, \q vivendo sozinhos \q num bosque perto da terra fértil do Carmelo. \q Deixa que eles se alimentem em Basã e em Gileade, como faziam muito tempo atrás.

decisions.choice: Shepherd your people: the prayer of the prophet for his people
decisions.reason: Verses 14-20 are a prayer to the LORD. The prophet asks the LORD to be the shepherd of his people, the role the ruler of 5:3 was promised (compare Psalm 28:9; 80:2). The LORD's answer seems to come in verse 15.

decisions.choice: the flock of your inheritance, dwelling alone: the LORD's own people, set apart
decisions.reason: Israel is the LORD's inheritance, the people that belong to him (Deuteronomy 9:29). "Dwelling alone" recalls Balaam's words, "a people dwelling alone" (Numbers 23:9; compare Deuteronomy 33:28): set apart, and safe. The staff is the shepherd's rod for guiding and protecting (Psalm 23:4).

decisions.choice: a forest in the midst of Carmel; Bashan and Gilead: the richest pasture lands
alternatives: in the midst of garden land
decisions.reason: Carmel is the wooded ridge on the coast, and its name also means garden land or orchard, so the line may mean "in the midst of fertile land". Bashan and Gilead, east of the Jordan, were famous for their pastures and herds (Jeremiah 50:19). They had been taken by Assyria (2 Kings 15:29). The prayer asks for the flock to graze again where it did "in the days of old".

decisions.choice: Shepherd (L, B); care for ... like a shepherd (R); the flock of your inheritance (L); the flock that belongs to you (B); your own flock (R); Carmel (all levels)
decisions.reason: All the "you" and "your" here are spoken to God and carry the setting for pronouns for God. Readable adds the address "LORD" so that it is clear who is spoken to (m1).

source.text: כִּימֵ֥י צֵאתְךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אַרְאֶ֖נּוּ נִפְלָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: As [in the] days of your going out from [the] land of Egypt I will show him wonders.

en.L: As in the days of your coming out from the land of Egypt, \q I will show him wonders.
en.B: As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, \q I will show them wonders.
en.R: I will do amazing things for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q as I did when they came out of Egypt.

pt.L: Como nos dias da tua saída da terra do Egito, \q eu lhe mostrarei maravilhas.
pt.B: Como nos dias em que saíste da terra do Egito, \q eu lhes mostrarei maravilhas.
pt.R: Vou fazer coisas maravilhosas pelo {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo, \q como fiz quando eles saíram do Egito.

decisions.choice: I will show him wonders: the LORD answers the prayer
alternatives: show us wonders: the prayer continues
decisions.reason: The verse speaks in the LORD's voice ("I will show"), answering verse 14. "You" is the people, addressed as one; "him" is the same people, spoken of as Israel. The change of persons is abrupt, and some read "show us", which would keep the prayer going.

decisions.choice: as in the days of the exodus: a second exodus of wonders
decisions.reason: The "wonders" are the signs the LORD did in Egypt and at the sea (Exodus 3:20; 15:11; Psalm 78:12). The prophets promise a new exodus, greater than the first (Isaiah 43:16-19; Jeremiah 23:7-8).

decisions.choice: your coming out ... show him (L); you came out ... show them (B); my people ... they came out (R); wonders (L, B); amazing things (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "them" for the people spoken of as "him"; Readable puts the people in the third person throughout and puts the comparison second.

source.text: יִרְא֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ וְיֵבֹ֔שׁוּ מִכֹּ֖ל גְּבֽוּרָתָ֑ם יָשִׂ֤ימוּ יָד֙ עַל־פֶּ֔ה אָזְנֵיהֶ֖ם תֶּחֱרַֽשְׁנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Nations will see and be ashamed of all their might; they will put a hand on [the] mouth; their ears will be deaf.

en.L: Nations will see and be ashamed, \q from all their might; \q they will put [their] hand on [their] mouth; \q their ears will be deaf.
en.B: The nations will see and be ashamed, \q for all their power; \q they will lay their hands on their mouths; \q their ears will be deafened.
en.R: The nations will see this and be ashamed, \q even with all their power. \q They will cover their mouths in shock. \q Their ears will go deaf.

pt.L: As nações verão e se envergonharão, \q de todo o seu poder; \q porão [a] mão sobre [a] boca; \q os seus ouvidos ficarão surdos.
pt.B: As nações verão e ficarão envergonhadas, \q apesar de todo o seu poder; \q porão a mão sobre a boca; \q os seus ouvidos ficarão surdos.
pt.R: As nações vão ver isso e ficar envergonhadas, \q mesmo com todo o poder que têm. \q Elas vão tapar a boca, espantadas. \q Os ouvidos delas vão ficar surdos.

decisions.choice: ashamed of all their might: their power will count for nothing
decisions.reason: When the nations see the LORD's wonders, all their power will seem shameful and useless to them. The words may also mean "ashamed, for all their might": in spite of it.

decisions.choice: a hand on the mouth ... deaf ears: speechless and stunned
decisions.reason: To put a hand over the mouth is to fall silent in awe or shame (Job 21:5; 40:4; Isaiah 52:15). Their ears will be as if deaf, stunned by what they have heard.

decisions.choice: see this (R); [their] hand on [their] mouth (L); in shock (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gesture means (m2).

source.text: יְלַחֲכ֤וּ עָפָר֙ כַּנָּחָ֔שׁ כְּזֹחֲלֵ֣י אֶ֔רֶץ יִרְגְּז֖וּ מִמִּסְגְּרֹֽתֵיהֶ֑ם אֶל־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ יִפְחָ֔דוּ וְיִֽרְא֖וּ מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: They will lick dust like the serpent, like crawling things of [the] earth; they will come trembling from their strongholds; to Yahweh our God they will come in dread, and they will be afraid of you.

en.L: They will lick dust like the serpent, \q like the crawling things of the earth; \q they will come trembling out of their strongholds; \q to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God they will come in dread, \q and they will fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: They will lick the dust like a serpent, \q like creatures that crawl on the ground. \q They will come trembling out of their fortresses; \q they will turn in dread to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God \q and will be afraid of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: They will crawl in the dust like snakes, \q like creatures that crawl on the ground. \q They will come out of their forts, shaking with fear. \q They will turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God in terror, \q and they will be afraid of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

pt.L: Lamberão o pó como a serpente, \q como os répteis da terra; \q sairão tremendo das suas fortalezas; \q {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, nosso Deus, virão com pavor, \q e terão medo de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}.
pt.B: Lamberão o pó como uma serpente, \q como os bichos que rastejam pelo chão. \q Sairão tremendo das suas fortalezas; \q com pavor se voltarão {{divine_name:para o SENHOR|para Javé}}, nosso Deus, \q e terão medo de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}.
pt.R: Elas vão rastejar no pó como cobras, \q como os bichos que rastejam pelo chão. \q Vão sair dos seus fortes tremendo de medo. \q Vão se voltar {{divine_name:para o SENHOR|para Javé}}, nosso Deus, apavoradas, \q e vão ter medo de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}.

decisions.choice: lick dust like the serpent: the deepest humiliation
decisions.reason: The serpent was cursed to eat dust (Genesis 3:14). To lick the dust is to lie face down before a conqueror (Psalm 72:9; Isaiah 49:23). The nations that mocked Zion will bow to the ground.

decisions.choice: to the LORD our God they will come in dread: the nations turn to him in fear
decisions.reason: Hosea 3:5 says that Israel will "come trembling to the LORD and to his goodness". Here the nations come trembling out of their fortresses to the LORD. The fear may be dread of judgment, or the awe that begins to worship, as in 4:1-2. In the last line the prayer speaks to God again ("you").

decisions.choice: the serpent (L); a serpent (B); snakes (R), as Genesis 3:14; strongholds (L); fortresses (B); forts (R)
decisions.reason: The word for the creature follows the published Genesis 3:14. Readable says what licking dust pictures: crawling in the dust in defeat (m1).

source.text: מִי־אֵ֣ל כָּמ֗וֹךָ נֹשֵׂ֤א עָוֺן֙ וְעֹבֵ֣ר עַל־פֶּ֔שַׁע לִשְׁאֵרִ֖ית נַחֲלָת֑וֹ לֹא־הֶחֱזִ֤יק לָעַד֙ אַפּ֔וֹ כִּֽי־חָפֵ֥ץ חֶ֖סֶד הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: Who [is] a God like you, forgiving iniquity and passing over transgression for [the] remnant of his inheritance? Not he holds on forever [to] his anger, for delighting in loyal love [is] he.

en.L: Who [is] a God like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, bearing iniquity and passing over transgression \q for the remnant of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance? \q He does not hold on to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger forever, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delights in loyal love.
en.B: Who is a God like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, who forgives wrongdoing and passes over rebellion \q for the remnant of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance? \q He does not keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger forever, \q because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delights in loyal love.
en.R: Who is a God like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? \q He forgives sin and overlooks the rebellion of the people who are left, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people. \q He does not stay angry forever, \q because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves to show faithful love.

pt.L: Quem [é] Deus como {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, que carrega a iniquidade e passa por cima da transgressão \q do remanescente da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} herança? \q Ele não se apega para sempre à {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tem prazer no amor leal.
pt.B: Quem é Deus como {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, que perdoa a maldade e deixa passar a rebeldia \q do remanescente da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} herança? \q Ele não guarda a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira para sempre, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tem prazer no amor leal.
pt.R: Quem é Deus como {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}? \q Ele perdoa o mal e não leva em conta a rebeldia do povo que restou, o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} próprio povo. \q Ele não fica irado para sempre, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} gosta de mostrar amor fiel.

decisions.choice: Who is a God like you? The question in Micah's own name
decisions.reason: Micah's name means "Who is like the LORD?", and the book ends by asking it. The Song of the Sea asks the same: "Who is like you among the gods, LORD?" (Exodus 15:11). Here what makes the LORD unlike any other is not only his power but his forgiveness.

decisions.choice: forgiving iniquity ... loyal love: the words of Exodus 34:6-7
decisions.reason: When the LORD passed before Moses he proclaimed himself "great in loyal love", "keeping loyal love to thousands, bearing iniquity and transgression and sin" (Exodus 34:6-7). Micah takes up the same words: bearing iniquity, transgression, loyal love, and in verse 19 compassion, and verse 20 adds faithfulness. Joel 2:13 and Jonah 4:2 also echo that passage.

decisions.choice: passing over transgression: overlooking it, not holding it against them
decisions.reason: To "pass over" an offense is to let it go (Proverbs 19:11). In Amos 7:8 and 8:2 the LORD said he would "never again pass by" Israel, that is, spare it; here he passes over the sin of the remnant. "The remnant of his inheritance" is the people that survives the judgment (2:12; 4:7; 5:6-7).

decisions.choice: he delights in loyal love: steadfast, faithful love is what he takes pleasure in
decisions.reason: *Hesed* is the loyal, faithful love that keeps a bond even when the other side has broken it. God's anger is real, but it does not last; his loyal love does (Psalm 30:6; 103:9; Isaiah 54:7-8).

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R)
decisions.reason: *Hesed* follows the wording set for the prophets, "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced and "faithful love" at Readable, here and in verse 20, pending the founder's ruling on the wording of Exodus 34:6, which these verses echo (the published Exodus has "steadfast love" at Literal and "faithful love" at Balanced and Readable). If that ruling settles one wording for every echo of Exodus 34:6, these verses follow it.

decisions.choice: bearing iniquity (L); forgives wrongdoing (B); forgives sin (R), as Exodus 34:7; transgression (L); rebellion (B, R)
decisions.reason: The phrase reuses its wording in the published Exodus 34:7 at each level. Readable joins the two lines into a statement after the question.

decisions.choice: Quem [é] Deus como tu (all levels); carrega a iniquidade (L), perdoa a maldade (B), perdoa o mal (R), as Exodus 34:7; amor leal (L, B), amor fiel (R)
decisions.reason: The question that echoes Micah's name (m1) keeps the words of Exodus 15:11 in Portuguese, "Quem [é] como tu", at every level. The words taken from Exodus 34:6-7 (m2) keep that passage's Portuguese per level ("carrega", "perdoa"), and hesed is "amor leal" at Literal and Balanced and "amor fiel" at Readable, as set for the prophets, here and in verse 20. The prayer moves from "tu" to "ele" as the Hebrew does.

source.text: יָשׁ֣וּב יְרַֽחֲמֵ֔נוּ יִכְבֹּ֖שׁ עֲוֺֽנֹתֵ֑ינוּ וְתַשְׁלִ֛יךְ בִּמְצֻל֥וֹת יָ֖ם כָּל־חַטֹּאותָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: He will again have compassion on us; he will tread down our iniquities; and you will cast into [the] depths of [the] sea all their sins.

en.L: He will again have compassion on us; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will tread down our iniquities; \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will cast into the depths of the sea all their sins.
en.B: He will again show us compassion \q and trample our wrongdoings underfoot. \q You will hurl all their sins into the depths of the sea.
en.R: He will be kind to us again. \q He will crush our sins under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet. \q You will throw all the sins of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people into the deepest sea.

pt.L: Ele voltará a ter compaixão de nós; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pisará as nossas iniquidades; \q e {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lançarás no fundo do mar todos os pecados deles.
pt.B: Ele voltará a mostrar compaixão por nós \q e pisoteará as nossas maldades. \q Tu lançarás todos os pecados deles no fundo do mar.
pt.R: Ele vai ser bondoso conosco de novo. \q Ele vai esmagar os nossos pecados debaixo dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés. \q Tu vais jogar todos os pecados do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo no fundo do mar.

decisions.choice: he will again have compassion: the tender love of Exodus 34:6
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word "compassionate" in Exodus 34:6, a love like a parent's for a child (Psalm 103:13). "Again" (literally "he will turn") means that he will turn back to them in mercy after his anger.

decisions.choice: tread down our iniquities ... cast all their sins into the depths of the sea: sin conquered and gone for good
decisions.reason: Sins are pictured as enemies, trampled underfoot, and then thrown into the deep where no one can bring them back. The words recall the sea that swallowed Egypt's army: "the depths covered them; they sank to the bottom like a stone" (Exodus 15:5).

decisions.choice: all their sins: as the Hebrew text has it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "their sins": the sins of the remnant (verse 18), the people who say "us". The ancient Greek translation and some other ancient versions read "our sins", matching "our iniquities". The prayer moves between speaking of God and speaking to him, and between "us" and "them", and the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: have compassion (L); show compassion (B); be kind (R); iniquities (L); wrongdoings (B); sins (R); all their sins (L, B); the sins of your people (R)
decisions.reason: The word for iniquity follows the wording set for the prophets. Readable says whose sins are meant (m3); "your" is spoken to God.

decisions.choice: no fundo do mar
decisions.reason: "O fundo do mar" is the plain Portuguese for the place no one brings things back from (m2), and is said at every level; "as profundezas" is the wording of the familiar versions.

source.text: תִּתֵּ֤ן אֱמֶת֙ לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב חֶ֖סֶד לְאַבְרָהָ֑ם אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֥עְתָּ לַאֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ מִ֥ימֵי קֶֽדֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: You will give faithfulness to Jacob, loyal love to Abraham, which you swore to our fathers from [the] days of old.

en.L: You will give faithfulness to Jacob, \q loyal love to Abraham, \q as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} swore to our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} from the days of old.
en.B: You will show faithfulness to Jacob \q and loyal love to Abraham, \q as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} promised our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} on oath long ago.
en.R: You will be faithful to the people of Jacob. \q You will show faithful love to the descendants of Abraham, \q as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} promised our {{gender:ancestors|forefathers}} long ago.

pt.L: Darás fidelidade a Jacó, \q amor leal a Abraão, \q conforme {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} juraste aos nossos {{gender:antepassados|pais}} desde os dias antigos.
pt.B: Mostrarás fidelidade a Jacó \q e amor leal a Abraão, \q como {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} prometeste com juramento aos nossos {{gender:antepassados|pais}} há muito tempo.
pt.R: Tu vais ser fiel ao povo de Jacó. \q Vais mostrar amor fiel aos descendentes de Abraão, \q como {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} prometeste aos nossos {{gender:antepassados|pais}} há muito tempo.

decisions.choice: faithfulness ... loyal love: the pair of Exodus 34:6
decisions.reason: The LORD is "great in loyal love and faithfulness" (Exodus 34:6), and the two words go together through the Psalms (Psalm 25:10; 89:15). Faithfulness is reliability, being true to one's word; loyal love keeps the bond. The book ends where verse 18 began, with the LORD's character.

decisions.choice: as you swore to our fathers: the oath to Abraham and Jacob
decisions.reason: The LORD swore to Abraham to bless him and his descendants (Genesis 22:16-18), and repeated the promise to Isaac and Jacob (Genesis 26:3; 28:13-15). Moses reminds Israel that the LORD keeps the oath he swore to their fathers (Deuteronomy 7:8, 12). Zechariah's song in Luke 1:72-73 recalls "the oath that he swore to our father Abraham".

decisions.choice: Jacob ... Abraham: the patriarchs and the people descended from them
decisions.reason: The names stand for the ancestors and also for their descendants, the people who bear their names. The promises made to the fathers are kept to their children.

decisions.choice: give (L); show (B, R); faithfulness (L, B); be faithful (R); loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R); swore (L); promised on oath (B); promised (R); ancestors (with the gender setting)
decisions.reason: *Hesed* follows the wording set for the prophets, pending the founder's ruling on the echoes of Exodus 34:6 (see verse 18). "Fathers" here means the ancestors of the people, so it takes the gender setting. Readable says that the names stand for the people (m3).
